posts.name: The Inner Circle Trader
posts.text:
Ladies & Gentlemen...

If you never read another post or lend your attention my way, take these words to heart.

The opinions, of others about you, should never shape who you are.  If you live your life like that, you will be led by emotions.

Greed and the pursuit to always please, impress, perform, or outclass someone else or something is a fools errand.

You won't convince everyone and no matter how many people claim to love you, believe in you, support you, promote you or what you stand for... the one person who doesn't and their weak words will disrupt your life.

None of you hold that measure of influence over me.  Yet, I see so many falling into traps via greed and image building .

I hold a seat of influence most would abuse.  A younger me might have abused it, I readily admit that.  You might read the trolls say I only trade paper accounts, I never trade live for others to copy me.

I can stand here among others who open themselves up to legal troubles by doing otherwise... and I say, I warned you.

I want each of you to find a model that works for you.  I would be thrilled to see all of you make millions.  However, the truth is, most of you are ill equipped to do it consistently.

Anyone who sits in front of others and leads them in live executions, opens themselves a direct pathway, in legal terms, for those who pay you.

Some of you laugh at my teaching style in paper trading, but you don't assume liability in demo accounts.  You never assume liability when you never provide "copy me" conditions for people who lack self-control or who are unable to manage impulsive behaviors.

You never assume liability if you don't sell affilate income with questionable practices.

I could have made more than all of the well known affiliate influencers combined, but I know the risks.  I never held or accepted an affiliate partnership that benefited me money wise.

Unfortunately, some of you who laughed under your breath, in my direction, will learn why I operate the way I do.

Don't allow money to influence commonsense and good judgement. 

A life with stress with lots of money in the bank is a broke life, so listen to good medicine. 

Hope this helps someone...

posts.name: Eva Fo𝕏 🦊 Claudius Nero's Legion
posts.text:
In early 2002, Elon was preparing to launch SpaceX and searching for the people who could help him build a rocket from scratch. One Sunday in January 2002, he walked into a friend's rented warehouse in Huntington Beach and found Tom Mueller holding an 80-pound rocket engine on his shoulder, trying to bolt it to a frame. It was the largest liquid-fuel engine any amateur had ever built, with 13,000 pounds of thrust, made in Tom's spare time. 

Elon asked the main question  “Could you build something bigger?”

The next Sunday Elon came to his house. It was Super Bowl Sunday; they watched maybe one play, because they were too busy sketching the first SpaceX rocket.

Tom became SpaceX employee #1, and the man who built engines on weekends went on to build Merlin, Kestrel and Draco. 

Elon saw a person, not a résumé, someone who built rockets with his own hands simply because he loved them.

posts.text:
No exchange can promise it will never be hacked again.

Bitget CEO Gracy Chen on prioritising transparency and users' interests, and why self-custody isn't risk-free either

"I can't really promise that there will never be another attack, and I believe no platform can responsibly promise that."

"For those who still want to take some time and think about how they custody their wallets, maybe from Ledger, you also realize self-custody has its own other set of issues."

"We can take a 300m-plus sort of hit as a company because we are pretty big. We are like top 3 or top 4 by trading volume globally among all the exchanges. But it won't be something a retail user can easily take or absorb."

"What I can promise is transparency, our professional ways of dealing with it, and again, put our users' interest in front of everything."

posts.name: Citrini
posts.text: Even if AI discovered these solutions today, it would take about 7-10 years to produce sufficient evidence they solve anything in humans. It’s going to speed some things up, and there’s really good work being done by people to try and facilitate that - but the amount of data we’d need to generate to reduce the timeline to a few years…I’m not going to say anything is impossible but we’d need to pretty much redirect every dollar of investing on AI infrastructure towards bio. If the pace of discovery accelerates beyond what we are used to (especially in diseases and targets where causal biology is well understood), I won’t be surprised at all. Like AI creating better immunotherapies I’d say is likely. AI curing cancer by 2030 would not just be surprising it would mean something massive (entirely outside of AI) had changed.

Crypto exchange volume dropped about 30% after the 10/10 crash

Bitget CEO Gracy Chen on where trading activity is moving, and why smaller exchanges were hit even harder

"Right after 10/10, we see a volume decrease of maybe 30% on average among all the top exchanges. For the smaller exchanges it could be even worse because there's like the Matthew effect."

"The big ones will become bigger, and the smaller ones will just shrink and become smaller and eventually die down. And that's indeed the situation that we've seen."

"What's quite interesting now that we are observing is a lot of users come to our platform to trade non-crypto assets. At its peak earlier this year, non-crypto assets counted for almost 40% of our total trading volume."

"One is tokenized commodities or commodity perpetuals, and the other one is stocks in general, especially US stocks."

posts.text:
Of the $388M stolen from Bitget, only $1-2M has been frozen so far

Bitget CEO Gracy Chen says crypto still struggles to trace stolen funds, while hackers shift from targeting keys to credentials

"They are more targeting credentials, processes, and trusted tools, rather than maybe originally mainly about private keys. Now we've done pretty good guarding of private keys, cold wallets, etc."

"But no exchange can address this alone. As an industry, we need to share intelligence around threats. We need to have a lot of fast coordination, especially when we are tracing illicit funds."

"On day one, you need to build your exchange with the mindset that they will be targeting you, especially if you grow bigger and have a lot of users and custodian funds."
